title: Spinach Fatayer with Sumac and Lemon
summary: Soft, golden triangular pies of olive-oil bread dough wrapped around a tangy spinach, onion, sumac and lemon filling.
equipment: large mixing bowl or stand mixer with dough hook

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed very dry
fine sea salt or table salt
lemon, cut into wedges, to serve

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, water and oil to a rough dough, then knead for 8 minutes by hand (5 in a mixer) until smooth, soft and springy. Kneading builds the gluten that lets the dough stretch thinly without tearing.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Cut the dough into 12 equal pieces (about 55 g each) and roll them into balls. Set them on a floured tray, cover and leave for 45-60 minutes, until puffy and soft.

steps.title: Filling
steps.text: Meanwhile, squeeze the spinach again in a towel, then mix it with the onion, sumac, lemon juice, oil, salt and chilli. The salt and acid draw out more water, so the filling should be moist but not dripping.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan), and line two baking trays with paper.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll each ball into an 11-12 cm round. Put about 30 g filling in the centre, lift the edge at three points and pinch the seams together firmly from the centre outwards to make a closed triangle. Firm pinching stops the seams opening in the oven.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Set the fatayer on the trays, brush them with oil and bake for 15-18 minutes, until golden. Serve warm with lemon wedges for squeezing.

tips: Wet spinach is the most common mistake: it makes the seams open. Squeeze it as dry as you possibly can.
Flour your fingers if the seams will not stick, and pinch hard.
Mix the filling just before shaping, so it stays dry.
They are good cold in a lunchbox.
storage: Keep in an airtight box in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat at 180 °C for 8-10 minutes. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
